A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]], $\sim$ an [[Definition:Equivalence Relation|equivalence relation]] on $X$, and $q: X \to X / \sim$ the [[Definition:Quotient Mapping|quotient mapping]].
Then $f: X / \sim \to Y$ is [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous]] {{iff}} $f \circ q$ is continuous.

B_source.statement:
Let $q: X \to X / \sim$.
The [[Definition:Quotient Topology|quotient topology]] declares $U \subseteq X / \sim$ open {{iff}} $\map {q^{-1} } U$ is open in $X$, the finest topology making $q$ continuous.

substitutions.the equivalence relation on the underlyi: the identification ~ on the points of X
substitutions.the finest compatible structure: the quotient topology, in which U is open iff its preimage is open
substitutions.a map out of the set-level quotient: a map f from X/~ to a space Y

derived.the set-level factorization: f corresponds to a ~-invariant continuous map on X
derived.continuity of f in terms of preimages: openness of f^{-1}(V) is by definition openness of (f . q)^{-1}(V)

validity_conditions: The quotient topology is defined so that a set is open in X/~ exactly when its preimage under q is open in X.
This makes q continuous and is the finest topology doing so, which is what makes the characterization an equivalence rather than one implication.
The stated criterion is then immediate, since the preimage of V under f and under f composed with q determine each other.
proof_plan: Take the set-level quotient $X / \sim$ with projection $q$.

As preimage commutes with unions and intersections, this is a [[Definition:Topology|topology]].
Any topology making $q$ continuous has every open $U$ satisfying $\map {q^{-1} } U \in \tau$, so this is the finest.

For $V \subseteq Y$ open:
:$\map {q^{-1} } {\map {f^{-1} } V} = \map {\paren {f \circ q}^{-1} } V$
Hence $\map {f^{-1} } V$ is open {{iff}} $\map {\paren {f \circ q}^{-1} } V$ is open, so $f$ is continuous {{iff}} $f \circ q$ is.
{{qed}}
